source.title: Mass Flow Choking
source.quote: Eq #10: mdot = (A * pt/sqrt[Tt]) * sqrt(gam/R) * M * [1 + .5 * (gam-1) * M^2 ]^-[(gam + 1)/(gam - 1)/2]

rows.note: Setting M=1 gives mdot = A*pt/sqrt(Tt)*sqrt(gam/R)*(2/(gam+1))^((gam+1)/(2(gam-1))). Sub-worker arithmetic for air (gam=1.4, R=287 J/kg/K): sqrt(1.4/287)=0.06984, (2/2.4)^3=0.5787, product 0.04042, so mdot = 0.0404*A*pt/sqrt(Tt) (SI) times Cd; at pt=101325 Pa, Tt=288 K this is about 241 kg/s per m2 of effective area. This arithmetic is the sub-worker's, not printed by the source.

rows.property: Rip panel geometry and effect on a helium aerostat

rows.product: tethered spherical helium aerostat (2.5 m test balloon)
rows.condition: covered by reinforced fabric; must be on the top of the envelope to avoid a sustainable zero-pressure balloon when open

source.title: The Design of Robust Helium Aerostats (MEng thesis)
source.quote: A rip panel consists of an opening in the aerostat, generally a slit that starts at the top of the balloon and runs 1/5th the circumference down, covered by a reinforced piece of fabric [10], [33]. source.title: Advisory Circular 91-71, Operation of Hot Air Balloons with Airborne Heaters
source.quote: Deflation Port. A panel in the top or side of a balloon envelope that, when opened/activated (sometimes referred to as “ripping out”), allows a large volume of air to escape from the balloon. It is normally used during landing and/or securing to eliminate the lift of the hot air and deflate the envelope.

gaps: FAA-P-8110-2 Airship Design Criteria (valve, ballast, emergency deflation, landing-load, landing impact text): not found online in openable form. Searches returned only AC 21.17-1/-1A (type-certification advisory circulars, downloaded, not the criteria) and the Transport Canada CAR 541 index (cites the document, no text). The FAA/LBA/RLD Transport Airship Requirements (TAR, March 2000), which derive from it, were opened instead and are the source of the airship rows.

TCOM, Lockheed Martin / ILC Dover aerostat rapid-deflation hardware and deflation times (seconds, hole area): no manufacturer page opened; only generic rip-panel descriptions (McGill thesis, LTA Solutions glossary, barrage-balloon article). No deflation-time number was read anywhere.
14 CFR 101 does not give a deflation time or a hole size for 101.19; no FAA advisory circular on the rapid-deflation device was found.

Choked-flow discharge coefficients for IRREGULAR/torn holes and cracks in thin plates: no primary source opened. Not opened or not reachable: ISO 5167, Perry's, Idelchik, Crane TP-410 (only cited inside NASA TM-103604), Shapiro 1953 (cited by LMNO), Kayser and Shambaugh 1991 paper (reported only via LMNO), NRC ML070860286 leak-rate appendix (HTTP 403), NASA TN D-5467 discharge coefficients of thick-plate orifices (downloaded; OCR too garbled to quote safely), NASA 1975 sharp-edged orifice chart reprint NTRS 19750049854 (link returned 404). A crack-flow paper (flashing flow through micro-slits, CNS proceedings) and a Heriot-Watt choked gas-liquid Cd paper were seen only as search snippets and are not recorded.

Spacecraft hull-breach REPRESSURISATION (inflow into an evacuated volume) time formula: no source found. Only depressurisation (outflow) material was read (space academy, NASA habitat paper). A choked-flow backfill time of an evacuated chamber is not given by any opened source; vendor/blog pages on vacuum venting and blowdown were seen only as snippets.

Heavy-balloon / punctured-balloon descent-speed data: none recorded. Search snippets (Nova-1 forum, Univ. Maryland Helios paper, Montana eclipse lesson, bexus.org) gave parachute-descent numbers around 4.6 to 9 m/s and a peak of 45 m/s, but none of those pages was opened, so no numbers are recorded.

Published landing-impact speed limits for airships or hot-air/gas balloons beyond 14 CFR 31.27(c) (36 in drop or max vertical velocity) and TAR 473(b) (3 ft/s floor): none found. No FAA maximum descent-rate limit for hot-air balloons was found (AC 91-71 only gives approach guidance).

Sphere drag at Re 1e5 to 1e7: Achenbach (J. Fluid Mech. 1972) was not opened (publisher page unreachable); values recorded are from Wikipedia, an MIT OCW note and a NASA K-12 page. No source gave a Cd for a rough/large-scale balloon at Re of 1e7.

Vacuum airship literature: no source opened discusses puncture, inrush, implosion or descent after a leak. The Akhmeteli and Gavrilin 2004-2007 patent publication (US 2006/0038062 A1) and the Univ. of Oregon 'Null Ship' thesis were not opened (Justia and Scholars Bank returned HTTP 403); the Wikipedia statement about the 2004-07 work was not recorded.

Wikipedia pages used as secondary sources for formulas and coefficients (choked flow, orifice plate, drag coefficient, drag crisis, added mass, barrage balloon, vacuum airship); their math is rendered as alt-text in the quotes.
